# A6 — Is the market geographically specialised? (short form)

*Draft, 2026-10-20 (panel day 44). Generated by `python -m analysis.a6_geography`; numbers in
`report/a6_results.json`. Cities come from `extraction/geography.py`, with Delhi, Gurugram, Noida,
Ghaziabad and Faridabad collapsed into NCR.*

## Answer

**This panel can't tell cities apart from employers, and once you compare within employers there's
no detectable specialisation.** The plan's four-city question shrinks to two cities: Bengaluru
(394 postings) and NCR (114). Hyderabad has 1 posting, Mumbai 14, Pune none. Pooled, the two cities
do differ in what they hire for (χ²(6) = 25.3, p = 0.0003): NCR has 1.6× its share of non-technical
roles and about half its share of infrastructure and data/ML roles. But **80% of NCR postings are
MongoDB's**. Shuffling city only *within* employers, which keeps each employer's own mix fixed,
leaves the difference well inside chance (p = 0.19). Among technical IC roles there's nothing to
explain even pooled (p = 0.51). **Remote work is an employer policy, not a property of the role**:
GitLab and Twilio list every India posting as remote, Okta 1%, Datadog none.

## Employer concentration (Herfindahl, 0–10,000)

| City | Postings | HHI | Largest employer | Technical IC: n, HHI, largest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bengaluru | 394 | 2,861 | Okta 48% | 206, 4,799, Okta 66% |
| NCR | 114 | **6,542** | MongoDB 80% | 43, **8,269**, MongoDB 91% |

The US Department of Justice treats an HHI above 1,800 as a highly concentrated market. Here, NCR
in this panel is effectively MongoDB's Gurugram office. That's the panel's limitation, not a claim
about NCR: the boards were chosen for API access, not to sample cities (see the coverage
limitation in [findings](findings.md)).

## Specialisation

Location quotients (a family's share in the city ÷ its share across both cities; >1 =
over-represented):

| Family | Bengaluru | NCR |
|---|---|---|
| Non-tech | 0.84 | **1.56** |
| Solutions | 0.95 | 1.17 |
| Software engineering | 1.06 | 0.78 |
| Data / ML | 1.11 | 0.61 |
| Product / design | 1.13 | 0.56 |
| Infrastructure | 1.16 | **0.46** |
| Other tech (QA, security) | 1.19 | 0.34 |

| Test | All postings | Technical IC |
|---|---|---|
| City × family, pooled χ² | 25.3, df 6, **p = 0.0003** | 2.3, df 3, p = 0.51 |
| Same statistic, city shuffled within employer (10,000 permutations) | **p = 0.19** | p = 0.78 |
| Postings at employers hiring in both cities (the only informative ones) | 371: Airbnb, Datadog, Elastic, MongoDB, Okta, OpenAI | 52: Airbnb, MongoDB |

A permutation test is used rather than Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel, because most employer-by-family
cells are tiny and an employer present in one city only should contribute nothing. Under the
within-employer shuffle it contributes nothing automatically.

The plan's standardised-residual breakdown isn't shown: with no difference left after adjusting for
employer, a cell-by-cell reading would only re-describe MongoDB's hiring mix.

## Remote share by family

Workplace known only (389 of 588 postings, so 34% unknown, mostly employer-driven):

| Family | Remote | Share (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|
| Data / ML | 11 / 19 | 58% (36–77%) |
| Other tech | 4 / 10 | 40% (17–69%) |
| Software engineering | 57 / 157 | 36% (29–44%) |
| Solutions | 16 / 46 | 35% (23–49%) |
| Infrastructure | 10 / 29 | 34% (20–53%) |
| Non-tech | 32 / 115 | 28% (20–37%) |
| Product / design | 3 / 13 | 23% (8–50%) |

By employer: GitLab, Twilio, Deepgram and Cloudflare 100% remote; Airbnb 41%; OpenAI 40%; MongoDB
5%; Okta 1%; Datadog 0%. The family differences overlap and track which employers hire each
family: 37% of data/ML postings with a known workplace are Twilio's (7 of 11 remote ones), against
8% of every other family's. Read the family table as the employer table in disguise.

## What would change my mind

- **More employers with offices in both cities.** Only two employers hire technical ICs in both
  Bengaluru and NCR. A real specialisation test needs a panel sampled to cover cities, for example
  Indian-HQ boards (Razorpay, Swiggy, Zomato). Those were ruled out mid-panel, so this is a
  next-panel design point, not a fix for this one.
- **Hyderabad and Pune** are where the plan expected contrasts, and the panel has no data on them.
